title: Pipelined Token Lease and NCCL Traffic Shaper for Predictable Prefill/Decode Overlap
creator: Marina Lopez
description: Background: Our prefills (long batched initial forward pass for KV population) frequently collide with downstream decode traffic on multi-GPU shards, causing large tail latencies and token reordering when NCCL saturates. Existing approaches we've tried (strict rendezvous windows and coarse microbatching) either underutilize GPUs or increase median latency. Goal: implement a lightweight, adaptive scheduling layer that acts like a 'token lease' allocator for pipeline/tensor stages and an NCCL traffic shaper that smooths inter-GPU allreduce/alltoall bursts. This should increase decode stability under prefill load without sacrificing throughput.
scope: Runtime scheduler + small runtime instrumentation; config knobs exposed to Dedicated customers and toggles in Private. No API changes. Deliver scheduling policy, two heuristics for lease sizing, kernel-hint propagation for attention paths, and an opt-in shaper that gates NCCL-heavy steps to avoid simultaneous bursts.
design_summary: 1) Token lease allocator: on a per-request basis the conductor grants a short-duration lease to a prefill microbatch on each pipeline stage. Leases contain: preferred start-window, soft priority, and an expiration timestamp. 2) NCCL traffic shaper: adds lightweight global token-bucket counters per-planner interval (configurable ms) to rate-limit NCCL calls that historically form spikes (alltoall/large allreduce). 3) Kernel selection hints: runtime propagates a hint upstream that indicates whether the current execution path should prefer memory-optimized kernels (for steady throughput) or latency-optimized kernels (for short, high-priority leases). 4) KV placement hinting: small affinity hint ensures most-recent KV segments for active leases are prefetch-friendly on local device to reduce cross-device fetches during decode.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- May slightly reduce peak throughput in favor of lower tail and higher predictability.
- Traffic shaping introduces added complexity in NCCL orchestration; risk of accidental serialization if bucket sizing is too conservative.
- Kernel-hint propagation requires tight coordination with the kernel selection layer; mismatch may cause suboptimal kernels being chosen.
- Edge cases: heterogeneous node bandwidth could make global shaper less effective; we fall back to topology-aware per-pod buckets.
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (spike): implement lease table and per-stage soft scheduler; no NCCL shaping yet.
Phase 2: add token-bucket shaper that monitors NCCL launch times and throttles start of heavy ops within a sliding window.
Phase 3: wire kernel selection hints through runtime metadata; provide metrics to surface hint efficacy.
Instrumentation: add new metrics: lease_wait_ms, lease_grant_rate, nccl_shaper_throttles, kernel_hint_mismatch_rate.
Fallback behavior: if shaper detects imbalanced throughput >30% across devices, auto-disable global mode and switch to per-topology buckets.
Test coverage: unit tests for allocator, integration tests with synthetic prefill/decode traces, and chaos tests with artificial link saturation.
acceptance_criteria: Tail P99 decode latency under concurrent prefill load reduced by >=25% on benchmark X (same model and workload as ENG-240001).
No regression >5% in median throughput for steady-state inference profiles.
Metrics emitted for all new scheduler signals and visible in Console dashboard under runtime-1.21 experiments.
Feature gated with runtime flag and documented in release notes; Dedicated customers can opt-in per-pool.
